mechanisms.title: Experience replay
mechanisms.question: Which old data are being reused?
mechanisms.summary: An environment transition remains useful for a conditional Bellman regression even when the behavior policy changes. A replay buffer mixes experience across time and permits multiple training updates per interaction.
mechanisms.distinction: PPO reuses one recent rollout for a bounded optimization phase. Its frozen old-policy probabilities and advantages serve a different purpose from long-lived off-policy replay. More updates per transition are not automatically more useful information.

uses.role: Stored state/action/reward/next-state trains Q; greedy target can differ from behavior.
Stored actions train Q; current actor actions at replay states train the actor.
Same data separation as DDPG; target actions are additionally smoothed.
Stored actions train Q; fresh current-policy actions at replay states train V and the actor.
Contrast: reuse the current rollout over K epochs, then collect a new rollout.

mechanisms.title: Target networks
mechanisms.question: Which learned quantities are allowed to move slowly?
mechanisms.summary: The critic predicts a label that itself uses learned values. A lagged copy slows how that label changes; stop-gradient separately fixes it during one optimizer step.
mechanisms.distinction: A target copy is not an independently trained second critic. Slow targets do not make a function approximator unbiased. Target updates copy or average weights; they are not backpropagation.

uses.role: One target Q; hard copy every C steps.
Same target copy, but online Q selects its next action.
Target actor + target Q; Polyak update after each training step.
Target actor + two target Qs; all update only in the delayed block.
Original 2018: target V only.
Later version: two target Qs, no V network and no target actor.

mechanisms.title: Bootstrapping
mechanisms.question: What estimate completes the target after the observed reward?
mechanisms.summary: TD replaces an unobserved future return with a current estimate. Each method specifies what next-state value is being evaluated.
mechanisms.distinction: This is distinct from policy improvement. Sharing a Bellman-regression critic does not make DDPG or SAC identical to discrete Q-learning.

uses.role: Next-state V of the evaluated policy.
Q at an actually sampled next behavior action.
Q averaged over target-policy next actions.
Maximum over next-action Q values.
Maximum over a delayed neural Q.
Target Q at target actor output.
Minimum of target Qs at a perturbed target actor action.
Target soft V: future reward plus future entropy.
Value bootstrap helps construct advantage/return targets, not the clipped ratio itself.

mechanisms.title: Double estimation / twin minimum
mechanisms.question: Who chooses the action, and who evaluates it?
mechanisms.summary: Action selection favors estimates that happen to be high. Separate estimators reduce that selection/evaluation coupling; a minimum adds a deliberately pessimistic choice.
mechanisms.distinction: Double Q, Double DQN, and clipped double Q are related but different. The minimum is neither an average nor a statistical confidence bound. Correlated critics can agree on the same mistake.

uses.role: Two tables: select with the table being updated, evaluate with the other.
One online Q selects; its target copy evaluates.
Two online critics + targets; use the target minimum for critic fitting, but Q1 for the actor.
Original SAC: minimum in both soft-V target and actor loss.
Later SAC: minimum in Q target and actor loss.

mechanisms.title: Score-function gradient
mechanisms.question: How does the probability of a recorded action change?
mechanisms.summary: Return or advantage weights the derivative of the log policy. The action is held fixed: this estimator does not need a differentiable reward or a derivative of Q with respect to action.
mechanisms.distinction: A Gaussian actor can use a score estimator or a pathwise estimator. The policy being stochastic does not decide this. PPO’s probability ratio is not the same operation as reparameterizing a new action.

uses.role: Sampled return, optionally minus a state baseline, weights the policy score.
A critic supplies a bootstrapped advantage estimate as the weight.
Parallel rollout advantages weight the same kind of score.
The likelihood-ratio surrogate is optimized with a trust-region step.
The old/new ratio and clipped surrogate gate this score signal.

mechanisms.title: Differentiate through action
mechanisms.question: How do weights move an action, and how does that change Q?
mechanisms.summary: The critic provides an action-space slope. The actor Jacobian maps that slope back to policy parameters. Critic weights stay fixed during the actor update, while its input remains differentiable.
mechanisms.distinction: This is not differentiation through the environment. “Frozen critic” and “detached Q output” are different: detaching the output would remove the Q-based actor signal.

uses.role: The deterministic policy-gradient theorem supplies the basic chain rule with policy occupancy.
Use a learned Q and replay states in a practical deep deterministic actor update.
Keep the same actor gradient, using Q1, but update it less frequently.
Hold noise fixed, transform it into a stochastic action, and differentiate both Q and log-density paths.

mechanisms.title: λ-return machinery / GAE
mechanisms.question: How much sampled future information supplies the learning signal?
mechanisms.summary: One-step TD, n-step returns, lambda-returns, and GAE arrange the tradeoff between sampled future outcomes and value bootstrapping.
mechanisms.distinction: GAE is an advantage estimator, not the PPO optimizer. Standard accumulating TD(lambda) and every online forward-view variant are not exactly interchangeable.

uses.role: Pick one sampled horizon before bootstrapping.
Mix horizons in the forward view; carry eligibility in the backward view.
Mix TD residuals into an advantage estimate.
Use fixed rollout advantages in the policy-ratio objective.

mechanisms.title: Control policy movement
mechanisms.question: What prevents repeatedly over-optimizing the same rollout?
mechanisms.summary: Even a locally useful policy-gradient estimate can become unreliable after the policy moves far from the distribution that generated the batch.
mechanisms.distinction: PPO’s clipped minimum is pessimistic relative to its unclipped surrogate. TD3’s minimum compares Q estimates. The shared word “pessimism” does not make them the same mechanism.

uses.role: Approximately enforce an average KL trust-region constraint.
Remove the sampled incentive for excessive beneficial ratio changes; no hard global ratio/KL bound.

mechanisms.title: Exploration behavior
mechanisms.question: What creates the actions sent to the environment?
mechanisms.summary: The behavior rule determines which transitions become available. Exploration and optimization can use different distributions in off-policy methods.
mechanisms.distinction: TD3 target noise never touches the environment. SAC’s policy randomness is part of its learned stochastic policy and objective, whereas DDPG/TD3 exploration noise is added to a deterministic actor.

uses.role: Epsilon-greedy or a UCB uncertainty bonus chooses actions to learn about rewards.
Epsilon-greedy over discrete Q values.
Sample the stochastic rollout policy; an entropy bonus can encourage diversity.
Add a separate exploration process, originally OU noise.
Add exploration noise independently of target-smoothing noise.
Sample from the learned stochastic policy; entropy affects learning too.

mechanisms.title: Entropy regularization
mechanisms.question: Is randomness a local bonus or part of the value being propagated?
mechanisms.summary: Entropy rewards a distribution for not collapsing too quickly. In maximum-entropy RL, future entropy contributes to the value of visiting a state.
mechanisms.distinction: SAC is not just PPO’s entropy bonus with replay attached. Its soft Bellman evaluation and actor objective are matched. The original and later SAC papers also differ in temperature treatment.

uses.role: Optional entropy bonus in the policy objective; usual V targets predict ordinary rewards.
Entropy appears in soft V and actor loss; original paper uses reward scaling / fixed temperature.
Entropy appears directly in Q targets; automatic temperature can match a target entropy.

mechanisms.title: Target policy smoothing
mechanisms.question: Could a narrow erroneous Q peak dominate the backup?
mechanisms.summary: Perturb the target actor’s next action, clip the perturbation and action bounds, then evaluate that neighborhood through repeated sampled backups.
mechanisms.distinction: The link to Expected SARSA is a mechanism analogy, not a claim that TD3 evaluates its exploratory behavior policy. One sampled perturbation per transition approximates the noise expectation over training.

uses.role: Average values under a specified target action distribution.
Use independently chosen smoothing noise around the target actor inside the Q backup.

mechanisms.title: Delayed improvement
mechanisms.question: How quickly should an actor chase a changing evaluator?
mechanisms.summary: Let the critic take more updates before using its slope to change the actor. TD3 delays target updates with the actor, slowing the feedback loop too.
mechanisms.distinction: The delay is a fixed update schedule. It does not check a convergence certificate. DDPG already had target networks; TD3 changes the relative timing and adds its other two controls.

uses.role: Baseline: actor and critic update in every training iteration.
Critics update each iteration; actor and all targets update every k iterations.
